CausalChain: In HCC, PCSK9 overexpression leads to degradation of LDLR on T cells -> Reduced LDLR impairs TCR recycling and T cell metabolic fitness -> Impaired T cell activation weakens anti-tumor immunity -> PD-1 blockade alone is insufficient due to suboptimal T cell function -> Pharmacological inhibition of PCSK9 restores LDLR levels -> Enhanced TCR recycling improves T cell activation and function -> Combined with PD-1 blockade, this synergy intensifies the antitumor response.
Hypothesis: Therapeutic inhibition of PCSK9 in HCC will restore LDLR-mediated TCR recycling on T cells, thereby enhancing T cell function and synergizing with PD-1 blockade to improve antitumor efficacy in patients with advanced hepatocellular carcinoma.
Abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a major clinical challenge due to inherent tumor heterogeneity and an immunosuppressive microenvironment that limits the efficacy of conventional therapies. Recent insights have highlighted non‐canonical roles of metabolic regulators including proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9) in modulating immune responses. Emerging studies suggest that PCSK9, by mediating the degradation of low‐density lipoprotein receptors (LDLR), may impair T cell receptor (TCR) recycling and thus dampen T cell activation. We propose that inhibition of PCSK9 may restore efficient TCR recycling and improve T cell metabolic fitness, thereby enhancing the activity of immune checkpoint inhibitors such as PD‐1 blockade. This combination strategy may act synergistically to overcome T cell dysfunction within the tumor microenvironment, providing a novel and testable therapeutic approach in advanced HCC.
